subject: Novamed Dedicated: finalizing SKU choice for low-latency + long-context
messages:
From: Cara Li <cara.li@novamed.ai>
To: ethan.park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@novamed.ai, procurement@novamed.ai
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated: SKU guidance + quick decision window

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting close on the procurement side and need to lock the SKU mix for our Dedicated pool so we can sign the reserve contract next month. A few things to make the recommendation concrete:

- Workload profile: mix of interactive chat (median request 1.5k tokens, 95th ~6k) + long-document summarization and vector search re-ranking where we sometimes pin full 65k-token contexts for batch jobs.
- Peak concurrency: expected 180 qps for chat at peak, with a batch window for long-context jobs that can run asynchronously.
- Latency target (chat): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms.
- Cost sensitivity: we'd prefer to push non-latency-critical tasks to cheaper routes but need predictable performance for chat.

We asked our infra team to attach an ML profile (see Novamed_ML_profile.csv). We're torn between committing to an H100-first pool vs an A100-heavy mix with L4 for cheaper bursts. Can you outline a recommended SKU split and the operational fallbacks (tiling, KV cache, reserve-to-burst policy) we should include in the SOW?

Also cc'ing procurement — if you can include a short note about billing/metric alignment (slots vs vGPU vs tokens) we can run with legal.

Appreciate a short write-up by EOD Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Cara
Cara Li
CTO, Novamed

Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated: SKU guidance + quick decision window

Cara —

Got the profile, thanks. High level up front: for a latency-first chat workload with occasional 65k contexts, a hybrid approach gives the best unit economics while preserving SLOs. Quick summary (details below):

- Primary pool: A100-80GB x ~40% of commit (handles most long-context requests without tiling).
- Latency tail and RLHF-like low-latency chat: H100 x ~40% (better FP16 throughput at low-latency tail).
- Cost/burst/embeddings: L4 x ~20% for non-critical bursts and cheap embedding traffic.

Operational fallbacks: prefix/kvcache for chat, automatic tiling for >40k token contexts (offloaded to batch L4 where possible), and slot-level routing by latency SLO (route to H100 first, fallback to A100 if out-of-capacity, and to L4 for best-effort).

I'll loop in ops and infra for a quick slotting matrix and reserve-to-burst recommendation. Kim / Irene — can you each add notes on node-count assumptions and autoscale/burst policy we should propose?

I'll draft a one-page SKU matrix and a short paragraph for procurement on how we meter/bill (covered tokens + reserved slot pricing + burst token surcharge).

—Ethan
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated: SKU guidance + quick decision window

Ethan / Cara —

I've run crude capacity math from the profile. Notes below are conservative (include 20% headroom):

1) Baseline service assumptions
- Chat service: median context 1.5k tokens, mean generation 180 tokens → ~30ms token-latency on H100, ~40–55ms on A100 depending on batch efficiency.
- 65k token jobs: impossible to keep in-memory on 40GB A100 without tiling; A100-80GB can hold them with smaller batch sizes but throughput suffers.

2) Recommended reserved pool (rounded) for commit of 180 qps peak:
- H100 nodes: 24 nodes (supporting low-latency chat p95)
- A100-80GB nodes: 20 nodes (handles pinned 65k contexts / background jobs)
- L4 nodes: 8 nodes (burst and embedding lanes)

3) Autoscale/burst config suggestions
- Reserve 70% of combined steady-state capacity on commit; allow burst to 130% using L4 spot-like instances for non-SLA traffic.
- Route decisions based on a latency-first policy: if H100 queue > 5s, progressive spill to A100; if A100 capacity exceeded and job is non-interactive, enqueue to batch L4.

4) Ops caveat
- For the 65k pinned contexts we recommend a small A100-80GB subpool pinned per-tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor eviction during batch windows.

I'll produce a short ops runbook (node counts, autoscale thresholds, monitoring alerts) and attach the spreadsheet to this thread.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Dedicated Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-proposed-sku-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)]
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated: SKU guidance + quick decision window

Quick infra sanity notes + tradeoffs —

- Memory vs throughput: A100-80GB is the simplest path for pinned 65k contexts (no tiling). But it increases reserved capacity cost per slot and reduces token/sec throughput vs H100 for the same dollars. H100 is superior for low-latency chat at scale (higher token/sec with optimized kernels) but requires careful memory-aware routing to avoid OOMs on large pinned contexts.

- Suggested pragmatic split for Novamed procurement language: commit to a blended pool with a graduated conversion clause after year 1: if 60%+ of traffic is latency-sensitive chat, allow up to 20% of reserved A100 capacity to be converted to H100 at pre-agreed rates. This reduces procurement friction and protects performance.

- Tiling & KV-cache: design calls for automatic tiling for >40k token contexts and persistent KV-cache warmers for frequent prefixes. Recommend we include an optional on-call ops add-on for the first 90 days to tune tiling thresholds.

I'll add rough cost deltas per node to the spreadsheet Irene attached and flag the change-log for procurement.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Cara —

Attaching the finalized one-page SKU summary and a procurement blurb (SLA/detour billing). Summary highlights:

- Recommended commit: 40% H100 / 40% A100-80GB / 20% L4. Node counts: H100 x24, A100-80GB x20, L4 x8 (see attached).
- Failover policy: latency-first routing, progressive spill to A100, enqueue to L4 for batch; emergency cross-region fallback if both H100/A100 are saturated.
- Billing note for procurement: reserved model = monthly fixed price per reserved node (covers baseline tokens), burst tokens billed at a discounted per-token rate, and a slot-conversion clause (see Kim's suggested conversion).

Next steps: if this looks good, reply-all with approval and procurement will issue an LOI. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the matrix tomorrow.

—Ethan
